key_insight: MuRF enables Vision Foundation Models to operate effectively across multiple input scales, letting them combine complementary strengths of low- and high-resolution views to produce stronger, scale-robust representations.
problem_solved: Current VFMs are typically run at a single fixed inference scale, failing to exploit complementary inductive biases from different resolutions (global context at low-res vs. fine detail at high-res).
method: Introduce a lightweight multi-scale inference framework that permits a VFM to ingest and aggregate features from multiple resolutions without re-training from scratch.
Use a compact fusion/aggregation mechanism to reconcile scale-specific features into a unified representation for downstream tasks.
Maintain compatibility with existing VFM weights to enable easy adaptation and efficient deployment across tasks and compute budgets.
impact: MuRF makes foundation models more flexible and robust by unlocking multi-scale information, improving downstream performance and deployment options while minimizing extra training cost. Practitioners can get better accuracy/robustness trade-offs and more adaptable inference strategies across vision tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing multi-scale inputs (low-res and high-res) feeding into a shared VFM and a fusion module producing a single output.
Before vs. After bar chart comparing single-scale inference performance to MuRF multi-scale performance on representative tasks (no exact numbers, relative improvement).
Heatmaps/feature maps illustrating global semantic clarity from low-res and fine detail from high-res, with arrows merging into a combined map.
Icon set for benefits: improved accuracy, robustness, compute-efficiency, and plug-and-play compatibility with existing models.
paper_title: MuRF: Unlocking the Multi-Scale Potential of Vision Foundation Models
paper_authors: Bocheng Zou, Mu Cai, Mark Stanley, Dingfu Lu, Yong Jae Lee
